_note: Test fixture. Every source here is fictitious and exists only to exercise the validators.
question: Does the Fixture Reading Programme improve reading comprehension for pupils aged 7 to 11?
purpose: Decide whether to pilot the programme in six schools next year.

inclusion: Comparison group or qualitative account of delivery
exclusion: Coverage of a study already included
protocol.synthesis_method: narrative synthesis with thematic synthesis of delivery evidence
assumptions: Comprehension measured by any standardised test counts as the outcome

sources.title: Fixture Trial One: a randomised trial in 58 schools
sources.authors: Fixture Author A; Fixture Author B
sources.context: 58 schools, 3,100 pupils aged 7 to 9, one school year, independent evaluator

sources.title: Fixture Trial Two: efficacy and twelve-month follow-up
sources.context: 12 schools, 640 pupils aged 8 to 11, follow-up at 12 months

sources.title: Fixture Review of structured reading programmes
sources.authors: Fixture Author D; Fixture Author E
sources.context: 14 trials of structured reading programmes; two concern this programme

concerns: Volunteer sample from schools still using the programme

sources.title: Fixture News: reading programme boosts scores
sources.exclusion_reason: Coverage of a study already included (S1)

claims.statement: The programme probably produces a small improvement in reading comprehension by the end of the first year.

support.text: Effect size 0.12 (95% CI 0.02 to 0.22) on a standardised comprehension test at one year
Effect size 0.21 (95% CI 0.05 to 0.37) on a standardised comprehension test at post-test
The two trials of this programme both favoured it, with effects below the review average

contradicts.text: District scores did not change in the two years after adoption
contradicts.reconciled: Before-and-after design with no comparison group, read only as a summary; weaker than the two trials.

claims.conditions: Pupils aged 7 to 11; delivery supported by the developer
claims.rationale: Two randomised trials agree in direction; lowered one level because the larger effect comes from a developer-led trial and the independent estimate is close to zero.

claims.statement: The improvement may not last: the one trial with follow-up found no difference at twelve months.

support.text: Effect size 0.03 (95% CI -0.14 to 0.20) at twelve-month follow-up
Few trials of structured programmes report follow-up, and effects usually shrink where they do

claims.rationale: One trial with high attrition at follow-up; the interval is wide enough to include a small lasting benefit.

claims.statement: Teachers found the daily sessions hard to fit into the timetable, and shortened them.

support.text: 11 of 16 teachers described shortening or skipping sessions because of timetable pressure
We did three a week, never five.

claims.rationale: A single qualitative study with a volunteer sample from schools that kept the programme.

claims.statement: A one-year pilot is reasonable only if it measures comprehension again a year after the programme ends and records how many sessions are delivered.
claims.rationale: Follows from a small probable benefit, doubtful durability and likely under-delivery; the step from evidence to pilot design is a judgement.
